meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'A champion is defined not by their wins but by how they can recover when they fall'?
meta.ogDescription: Serena Williams really said it — the popular line trims her fuller 2012 remark to The National, given during her comeback from a life-threatening illness.

answer.label: Spoken by
answer.sourceLine: She really said it. The line you usually see is the trimmed form of a fuller remark — “I really think a champion is defined not by their wins but by how they can recover when they fall. I have fallen several times…” — documented in a 2012 interview with The National ↗, spoken during her comeback from a life-threatening 2011 illness. The popular version simply drops her opening “I really think.”

source.excerpt: I really think a champion is defined not by their wins but by how they can recover when they fall. I have fallen several times. Each time I just get up and dust myself off and I pray, and I’m able to do better or I’m able to get back to the level that I want to be on.
trail: The fuller quotation is reported in a 2012 interview with The National ↗, tied to her return after her 2011 health scare.
Essence ↗ reproduces the passage word-for-word and credits that same interview with The National.
The circulated one-liner appears across quote databases such as Goodreads ↗, usually without the “I really think” opener or the source.
It is not in the sourced section of Wikiquote ↗, so news reporting remains the best available citation.

author.bio: Serena Williams (born 1981) is one of the greatest tennis players in history, holding 23 Grand Slam singles titles — the most in the Open Era. Her career included a near-fatal pulmonary embolism in 2011 and a celebrated return to dominance, the very context in which this remark about recovery was spoken.

misattribution.heading: The wording, and how it travels
misattribution.intro: This one is genuinely hers — the issue is not who said it but how completely it’s quoted. The internet has sanded a fuller sentence down to a tidy motto.

items.why: “A champion is defined not by their wins but by how they can recover when they fall” drops her opening “I really think” and the follow-on — “I have fallen several times” — that gave the line its personal weight, per The National ↗.
Some sites render it as “A champion is not defined by their wins but how they recover when they fall,” a light paraphrase that reorders her words — the meaning survives, the exact phrasing does not.

misattribution.truthLine: Bottom line: Serena Williams really said this. The clean motto is a faithful trim of her fuller 2012 remark to The National ↗, not a fabrication.

context.heading: Why she said it
lead: Williams made the remark during her comeback from a 2011 pulmonary embolism — a blood clot in the lungs that can be fatal — which had sidelined her for nearly a year. Read against that, “how they can recover when they fall” is not a slogan but a description of what she had just lived through.

That autobiographical anchor is exactly what the trimmed motto loses. The full sentence continues, “I have fallen several times,” making clear she was speaking about herself, not issuing a general maxim.
context.pull: A champion is defined… by how they can recover when they fall.
